judged_text: symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse run with no try/catch and the decrypted value is persisted without validation against the app's credential schema, so a wrong-key or malformed payload throws into a 500 while any decryptable JSON value is written as the credential key and acknowledged with 200. A parent/child encryption key mismatch turns every sync delivery into an unhandled 500, and a malformed-but-decryptable payload silently replaces a working credential with garbage while returning 200, so the sender believes sync succeeded and the user's integration is bricked without any error signal.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is handled as `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no `try/catch` or validation. If the encryption key is wrong/missing or the ciphertext is malformed, `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` can throw, which will bubble up as an unhandled error (500) because the handler does not catch it. Also, any decryptable JSON value is written directly to `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update/create` without validating shape against any app credential schema (only the outer webhook body is zod-validated), so a malformed-but-JSON payload can overwrite a previously working credential while the endpoint still returns 200.
